key_risks.description: Gross margin compression: gross margin fell 160 basis points to 49.8% in the quarter on higher commodity costs, product and packaging investments and unfavorable product mix. Pricing contributed only 20 basis points, and manufacturing productivity and lower tariff costs did not fully offset the pressure.

Commodity, energy and Middle East-linked input cost inflation could persist. The filing says input costs (energy and other commodities) are primary drivers of gross margin, and management has sized a roughly $1 billion after-tax cost headwind into its fiscal 2027 outlook, tied to oil prices.
Price elasticity: the filing notes that increased pricing to offset inflation or cost increases may negatively impact product consumption, limiting the ability to recover margin through price.

Rising short-term leverage and thin liquidity cushion: debt due within one year rose to $17,028 million from $11,296 million at June 30, 2026, and current liabilities exceeded current assets by about $12.5 billion. Net short-term debt additions of $5,758 million funded the cash build ahead of the Thorne acquisition.

Debt-funded M&A and higher interest cost: the $3.9 billion all-cash Thorne acquisition closed October 1, 2026, after the quarter end. Interest expense rose $26 million to $223 million, and interest income fell $6 million.

Working capital quality: operating cash flow benefited from a $1,149 million payables inflow in the quarter, while accounts receivable (-$589 million) and inventories (-$349 million) consumed cash. A reversal of payables timing would weaken cash conversion.

Restructuring execution risk: the company is executing a multi-year restructuring program with overhead reductions and go-to-market discontinuations. Savings must show up in margins while wage inflation and restructuring costs continue to run through the P&L.
Market share losses in several categories, including Beauty, Oral Care, Grooming and Fabric Care, with competitive activity cited in North America and Europe. Health Care unit volume declined.
Tax rate volatility: the effective tax rate rose to 21.0% from 20.8% on discrete impacts related to uncertain tax positions, and other non-operating income fell $61 million year over year.

bull_case: Volume is leading growth: net sales rose 4.0% to $23.3 billion in the quarter on 2.4% unit volume growth, which is a healthier basis for a staples franchise than price-led growth.

Productivity savings and overhead discipline delivered 130 basis points of SG&A leverage, taking SG&A to 24.3% of sales (down 90 basis points) and holding total SG&A flat at $5.7 billion, which helped operating income grow 1% to $5.9 billion despite gross margin pressure.

Cash generation remains strong: Q1 operating cash flow was $5,767 million versus $5,408 million a year ago, and free cash flow of roughly $4.4 billion covered the $2.6 billion dividend and $1.25 billion of buybacks.

Cash and cash equivalents rose to $15.4 billion. Net debt of about $23.6 billion was slightly below the roughly $24.2 billion at June 30, 2026, so leverage did not rise even after pre-funding the Thorne deal.
Beauty net sales grew 6% to $4.4 billion with innovation-led volume growth in Europe, Asia Pacific and Greater China, and Grooming grew 4% with earnings before tax up 6%.

A defined restructuring program (about $2.0 billion over two years, up to 7,000 overhead roles by end of fiscal 2027) is sized and time-bound, and could reset the cost base if commodity and investment headwinds ease.
The 0% to 3% core EPS growth guide for fiscal 2027 could prove conservative if volume holds and gross margin troughs on schedule, although this depends on the cost outlook.
Thorne adds a premium health and wellness franchise, and the long-term algorithm of mid-to-high single-digit core EPS growth and 90%+ adjusted FCF productivity is retained.
bear_case: Gross margin fell 160 basis points to 49.8% on 140 basis points of commodity costs, 140 basis points of product and packaging investment and 50 basis points of unfavorable mix, against only 20 basis points of pricing benefit. Incremental operating margin was only about 9% (operating income +$81 million on sales +$890 million).

Core EPS grew only 1% to $2.00 on 4% sales growth, and net earnings fell 1%, so volume is not converting to profit at the historical rate. Diluted EPS rose 1% to $1.97 mainly because of a lower share count.

Pricing power is thin (0.4% price contribution in the quarter, 1% in fiscal 2026), and the filing warns price increases may hurt consumption. Growth looks to be bought with trade and product investment.
SG&A leverage largely reflects scale and flat dollar spend ($5.7 billion) rather than lower absolute costs, so it may not be repeatable as the cost-cutting runway shortens.

The balance sheet is more stretched: debt due within one year rose to $17.0 billion from $11.3 billion, current liabilities exceed current assets by about $12.5 billion, and the $3.9 billion all-cash Thorne deal plus a roughly $5.0 billion buyback were partly debt-funded. Interest expense rose $26 million to $223 million.
Fiscal 2026 operating income fell 3% to $19.7 billion and operating margin fell 160 basis points to 22.7%, so the margin trend predates the latest quarter.
Share losses in Oral Care (-0.6 points), Grooming (-0.4) and Fabric Care (-0.4), a Beauty share decline of 0.3 points, and Health Care volume down 2.9% suggest erosion in core categories.

The roughly $1 billion after-tax cost headwind in the fiscal 2027 guide is tied to elevated oil prices, leaving little cushion if energy stays high. Analyst price-target cuts suggest the market is already pricing that risk.

what_to_watch.text:
**FY2027 Guidance and Margin Trough Timing:** Management guides to core EPS of $6.89 to $7.11 (0% to 3% growth) and organic sales growth of 1% to 3%. Unit volume grew 2.4% in the quarter and productivity delivered 130 basis points of SG&A leverage, which supports the view that the guide could prove conservative if commodity and product-investment headwinds ease. That said, gross margin still fell 160 basis points with pricing adding only 20 basis points against 140 basis points of commodity and 140 basis points of product and packaging investment, and part of the SG&A leverage is simply scale on flat $5.7 billion spending. The case for upside therefore depends on a margin trough that the reported numbers do not yet show.

-> Monitor whether management reaffirms or raises the core EPS range and how it sequences gross margin recovery through the remaining quarters.

**Gross Margin Bridge:** Gross margin declined 160 basis points to 49.8% (140 basis points commodities, 140 basis points product and packaging investment, 50 basis points mix), and fiscal 2026 gross margin fell 100 basis points to 50.2%. Incremental operating margin of only about 9% shows volume is not dropping through to profit, and the commodity headwind widened through fiscal 2026 from roughly $100 million to $150 million after tax. On the other hand, manufacturing productivity and lower tariff costs (50 basis points) partially offset the pressure, and SG&A leverage cushioned operating income growth of 1%.

-> Monitor the basis-point gross margin bridge, the pace of pricing versus commodity costs, and any change to the commodity and tariff cost estimates on the call.

**Capital Return Funding and Balance Sheet:** Q1 operating cash flow of $5,767 million less capex of $1,366 million left about $4.4 billion of free cash flow against $2.6 billion of dividends and $1.25 billion of buybacks, and net debt of about $23.6 billion is slightly below the roughly $24.2 billion at June 30. However, debt due within one year rose to $17.0 billion from $11.3 billion, total debt rose by about $4.8 billion to roughly $38.9 billion, current liabilities exceed current assets by about $12.5 billion, and the $3.9 billion Thorne deal and roughly $5.0 billion FY2027 buyback must be financed alongside the dividend. The $4.8 billion 364-day backstop facility expires in October 2026 and is undrawn.

-> Monitor the fiscal 2027 free cash flow bridge, commercial paper and refinancing commentary, the renewal of the 364-day facility, and any net debt target.

**Quality of Growth: Price, Volume and Mix:** Net sales grew 4.0% with 2.4% from volume, 1.1% from mix and only 0.4% from price, and fiscal 2026 pricing was just 1%. Volume-led growth is generally healthier than price-led growth, and product and packaging investment may pay back through share and scale. That said, the 1.1% mix contribution is described as geographic mix, and unfavorable product mix cost 50 basis points of gross margin in the quarter. The risk is that growth is being bought with trade and product investment while margins absorb the cost.

-> Monitor organic volume versus pricing by segment, trade investment commentary, and the pricing actions planned in response to input cost inflation.

**Energy and War-Related Cost Headwind:** Management's fiscal 2027 outlook embeds roughly $1 billion after tax of higher raw material, energy and transportation costs, based on an assumed Brent crude price of $90 a barrel. The Street's default view is that this normalizes if energy markets calm, and the restructuring is meant to offset part of it. However, the cost is explicitly tied to oil staying elevated, so it is a run-rate headwind if oil stays high, and TD Cowen cut its price target to $142 from $156 on this risk.

-> Monitor management's updated oil price assumption, the size of the cost headwind versus the $1 billion estimate, and pricing or surcharge actions.

**Restructuring Payoff and Reinvestment:** The program targets about $2.0 billion of before-tax costs over two years and up to 7,000 non-manufacturing overhead roles by the end of fiscal 2027, with a guided 30 to 50 basis point headwind in fiscal 2027. Overhead costs fell 70 basis points as a percentage of sales and Q1 free cash flow productivity was 93%, but marketing spending rose in dollars, so savings are being recycled into brand support rather than margin. The historical run-rate for restructuring is only about $250 to $500 million a year, so the program is large relative to normal activity, and cash restructuring costs remain to come in fiscal 2027.

-> Monitor cumulative restructuring charges, realized overhead savings, and whether SG&A as a percentage of sales continues to fall with flat dollar spend.

**Beauty Momentum Versus Core Category Share Losses:** Beauty net sales grew 6% to $4.4 billion in the quarter, with innovation-led volume growth in Europe, Asia Pacific and Greater China, and Grooming grew 4%. However, Beauty segment net earnings fell 1% and its share declined 0.3 points, while Oral Care lost 0.6 points of share, Grooming 0.4 and Fabric Care 0.4, and Health Care volume fell 2.9% on competitive activity. The long-term algorithm of mid-to-high single-digit core EPS growth depends on premium mix outgrowing share erosion in mature categories.

-> Monitor segment-level volume, share changes and margin in Beauty, Health Care and Fabric Care.

**Thorne Integration and Interest Cost:** The $3.9 billion all-cash Thorne acquisition closed on October 1, 2026, and was funded largely with a net debt increase, with interest expense up $26 million to $223 million in the quarter. The deal adds a premium health and wellness franchise, and the net debt effect has so far been limited because cash was built ahead of closing. That said, the added purchase price comes on top of dividends and a roughly $5.0 billion buyback, while core EPS growth is guided to only 0% to 3%, leaving little room for dilution.

-> Monitor Thorne's expected contribution to sales and EPS, purchase accounting and amortization effects, and any change in net interest expense guidance.
